root_cause.text: The mt76 DMA cleanup path failed to free page_pool-backed RX buffers for certain RX queues because `mt76_dma_cleanup()` skipped WED RRO queues entirely and `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` did not return pages for non-NAPI/WED RRO queue types, causing a memory leak on device/module unload.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `continue` in `mt76_dma_cleanup()` that previously skipped `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` for `mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) && mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)`, and adds logic in `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` to either skip only active WED RRO queues or call `mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false)` for queues that are not `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c(q)` and not `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind(q)`, matching the commit message that “All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not associated to a NAPI” and that the page_pool must be destroyed during cleanup.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `continue` in `mt76_dma_cleanup()` that previously skipped `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` for `mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) && mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q)`, and adds logic in `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup()` to either skip only active WED RRO queues or call `mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false)` for queues that are not `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c(q)` and not `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind(q)`, matching the commit message that “All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not associated to a NAPI” and that the page_pool must be destroyed during cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix RX cleanup to avoid releasing buffers for active WED RRO queue types that are managed by hardware.
intent_record.what: In mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(), the existing single check `if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q))` was replaced with a new conditional that first skips processing when WED is active and the queue is WED RRO, and then only calls `mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false)` when the queue is neither `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c(q)` nor `mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind(q)`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes which RX buffers are returned to the page pool during cleanup. Buffers for certain WED/RRO queue types are no longer released through the normal page-pool path, preventing incorrect cleanup for hardware-managed queues while preserving release for non-WED or non-specialized queue types.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always clean up RX NAPI and DMA queues during mt76_dma_cleanup(), including WED RRO queues.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a conditional block from mt76_dma_cleanup() that previously skipped NAPI deletion and RX queue cleanup when mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) was true and mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q) returned true.
intent_record.how: After this change, all RX queues in the loop are always passed to netif_napi_del() and mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(), regardless of whether the WED device is active or the queue is a WED RRO queue. This changes teardown behavior so those queues are no longer exempt from cleanup in this function.

grouping_result.intent: Always clean up RX NAPI and DMA queues during mt76_dma_cleanup(), including WED RRO queues.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix RX cleanup to avoid releasing buffers for active WED RRO queue types that are managed by hardware.
consistency_review.reason: Hunk 0 is about preventing premature buffer release for hardware-managed WED RRO RX queues, while Hunk 1 instead adds broader cleanup of RX NAPI and DMA queues during mt76_dma_cleanup(); these are related to RX teardown but implement different behaviors and purposes, so they do not form one coherent change.

relevance_review.reason: The change targets RX cleanup for WED RRO queues, which is directly related to the reported leak in DMA cleanup for page_pool-backed RX buffers on those queue types.
The change directly matches the reported leak: it ensures mt76_dma_cleanup() also cleans up WED RRO queues, which were previously skipped and left page_pool-backed RX buffers unreleased on unload.

candidates.rationale: This pre-fix conditional caused mt76_dma_cleanup() to skip cleanup for active WED RRO RX queues, leaving their buffers/page_pool allocations unreleased during unload.
Together with the preceding condition, this identifies WED RRO queues as the ones being skipped entirely, which directly leads to the leak on cleanup.
This condition gated page_pool buffer release in mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(), so non-NAPI/WED RRO queue cleanup could fail to return pages, causing leaked RX buffers.
This is the actual buffer-return operation that was conditionally skipped for affected queues, so the leak manifests when this statement is not reached.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition caused mt76_dma_cleanup() to skip cleanup for active WED RRO RX queues, so their page_pool-backed buffers were not released on unload.
Together with the preceding condition, this identifies the WED RRO queues that were excluded from cleanup entirely, leading to the memory leak.
This guard prevented mt76_dma_rx_cleanup() from returning page_pool buffers for the affected queue type, so RX pages were leaked.
This is the actual buffer release operation that was conditionally skipped for the vulnerable queue paths, resulting in unreleased RX buffers.
